nodes.title: Screen before joining the repair queue
nodes.detail: Accept only clean, portable, low-risk items within the repairer’s competence and available time. Decline powered items and safety-critical, contaminated or hazardous work. Record the item, fault, risks, agreed work and consent; repairer confirms triage before starting. One item per person; no promise of repair.
nodes.authoredText: Screen before joining the repair queue Recommended acceptance: clean, dry, portable textiles or non-powered household items; visible, low-risk fixes achievable with hand tools, safe workholding, available materials, time and the assigned repairer’s skills. Examples: a hem, button or simple non-load-bearing fitting. Decline/referral: powered items; gas, fuel, pressure or stored-energy hazards; leaking/swollen batteries; contamination, pests or exposed shards; structural/load-bearing repairs, medical devices, protective equipment, child-safety products or other failures that could cause serious injury. Do not open hazardous items to “take a look.” These are conservative event limits, not universal bans. Triage and consent: intake records item ID, owner, fault/history, existing damage and known hazards. Repairer confirms scope before work. Explain possible damage, incomplete repair, no guarantee and the right to stop; obtain informed agreement before disassembly or changing scope. Offer a verbal/read-aloud explanation; do not treat a signature as proof of understanding. Keep only needed personal data securely. Queue: one item per person, separate queues by skill, owner stays available, no unattended drop-offs. Coordinator caps waiting to room capacity and remaining repair time; stop intake before the final work/check/cleanup window. Set that cutoff in the briefing; do not promise throughput. Repair Café International’s house rules support refusal, one-item queues and no repair guarantee. They do not establish an enforceable local liability waiver; confirm consent wording and insurance locally.

nodes.title: Control work, stopping and release
nodes.detail: Keep accessible routes and exits clear, contain tools and sharps, supervise participation and preserve safety coverage. Stop on hazards, uncertainty, fatigue or inadequate time. Record work and checks; return items with limitations and unsafe-use warnings. Follow venue emergency procedures and record incidents and near misses.
nodes.authoredText: Control work, stopping and release Room: preserve clear, lit routes from entrance through intake, tables, toilets and exits; include turning space, seated waiting and reachable work positions. Keep bags and cables off routes, tools behind the work boundary, and needles/sharps contained and counted. Use stable tables, safe workholding and task-appropriate eye protection. No hot work, sprays or solvents under this baseline. Keep children with a responsible adult; participation requires repairer supervision. Stop: anyone may call a halt for unexpected hazards, unsafe tools, uncertain competence, crowding, fatigue or insufficient time to leave the item safe. If safety/first-aid cover is diverted, pause affected work. Only the coordinator and relevant repairer restart after the cause is controlled. Release: repairer records work, checks actually performed and outcome: repaired, partial, unrepaired or unsafe. Explain remaining limits; label unsafe items “do not use” and refer onward. Secure loose parts/sharps and return to the identified owner; never describe a functional check as safety certification. Incident: stop and protect people, alert library staff, use agreed emergency/evacuation procedures and obtain first aid or emergency help. Record facts, time, item, injury/near miss and action; secure evidence and notify the venue/insurer under agreed rules. Check statutory reporting locally before reopening. Verified guidance: HSE recommends proportionate emergency plans, clear roles, unobstructed exits and visitor first-aid assessment. US DOJ accessible-meeting guidance (archived) covers routes, room arrangement and restrooms. The specific operating rules above are recommendations for this café.

nodes.authoredText: Start small: two stations, eight initial slots Run textile mending and simple non-powered household fixes , with two volunteers at each bench, one on intake and one coordinating. This preserves help for arrivals, safe decisions and overruns. Suggested afternoon: 30 minutes to set up and brief; 2½ hours open; 30 minutes to pack and debrief. Adjust to the actual room booking. Close intake 30 minutes before public closing, or earlier if the queue fills. Start with eight slots: four per bench . Allow about 30 minutes each, leaving buffer within the open period. Stagger arrivals; add walk-ins only when skills, time and room capacity allow. This is a planning estimate, not guaranteed throughput. Before advertising: confirm skilled bench leads, permitted activities, room capacity/access, insurance, first aid and emergency arrangements with the library. Narrow or postpone the event if these cannot support it. No powered, hot-work or safety-critical repairs. Supply budget: unresolved. Inventory available or loanable tools and consumables first; availability is unconfirmed. No spend, free supplies or purchases are assumed.

nodes.title: Six volunteer roles
nodes.detail: Volunteers 1–2: textiles, including hems, buttons and small patches. Volunteers 3–4: simple non-powered household fixes. Volunteer 5: intake, consent and tickets. Volunteer 6: coordinator, queue, library liaison and safety oversight. Each bench needs a competent lead; helpers do not create additional repair slots. Preserve intake and coordinator cover during breaks.
nodes.authoredText: Allocate the six volunteers People Role and work 1–2 Textiles: competent lead plus helper; buttons, hems and small patches using hand sewing. 3–4 Household: competent lead plus helper; simple non-load-bearing fittings and loose handles on portable, non-powered items. 5 Intake: screen, explain rules, record consent, issue tickets and route by skill. 6 Coordinator: queue, library liaison, safety oversight, incidents and break cover. Operate one repair at a time per bench , with visitors learning alongside the repairer. If a skilled lead is unavailable, reduce the advertised scope. Stagger short breaks. The coordinator may cover intake only with a named competent deputy for coordination and safety; otherwise pause intake or affected work. A helper is not automatically qualified to lead. Inventory before committing: sewing kit, scissors, screwdrivers, pliers, suitable workholding, task-appropriate eye protection, table covers, labels and intake sheets. First-aid provision must be agreed with the library. No budget or tool availability is assumed.

nodes.title: Intake and safe handback

Explain risks and no guaranteed repair; obtain informed agreement. Decline powered, hazardous and safety-critical work. Anyone may stop unsafe work. Record outcomes and checks, return all parts and explain remaining risks.
nodes.authoredText: A short intake-to-handback routine Screen: one clean, dry, portable item per visitor; owner stays available. Record item ID, owner, fault/history, condition and hazards. The repairer confirms skills, materials and time before acceptance. Agree: explain the proposed work, possible damage, incomplete repair and no guarantee; obtain informed agreement before disassembly or changing scope. Offer a read-aloud explanation. Collect only necessary personal data. Decline: powered items, batteries with damage or leakage, fuel/pressure hazards, contamination, exposed shards and safety-critical or load-bearing work. No plug-in diagnosis, hot work, sprays or solvents. Control and stop: keep accessible routes and exits clear; contain needles and tools; supervise participation and keep children with an adult. Anyone may stop for hazards, uncertainty, fatigue or insufficient safe finishing time. Pause if intake or safety cover is lost; use library emergency procedures for incidents. Hand back: record work, checks and outcome; return parts securely to the owner. Explain remaining faults, label unsafe items “do not use” and refer onward. A functional check is not safety certification. The focused review supports this approach. Venue and competence have not been inspected; local requirements and insurance remain to be confirmed. Repair Café house rules support one-item queues, refusal and no repair guarantee. Intake and safety review

nodes.authoredText: Keep coverage; reduce the initial offer Provisional recommendation: one paired repair bench for the afternoon, preferably hand-sewn mending—buttons, hems and small patches—if a competent lead stays. If staying skills favour household fixes, offer only simple non-powered, non-load-bearing work instead. Two staying volunteers: repair lead and helper. One: intake, consent and tickets. One: coordinator, queue, library liaison and safety oversight. One: floater for tools, arrivals and trained break cover. Short-shift sixth person: setup and arrival support; no role that must continue after departure. Brief and hand over before they leave. Keep the suggested 30-minute setup, 2½-hour public window and 30-minute closeout, subject to the room booking. Start with four 30-minute repair slots , replacing eight; this leaves 30 minutes of buffer. Close intake 30 minutes before public closing, or sooner if full. Slots are estimates, not repair guarantees. Tradeoff: fewer items and less choice, but paired work and break cover remain. A two-bench alternative is one skilled textile repairer + two household repairers + intake + coordinator ; use it only if both leads stay, textile tasks are safe solo, and breaks can be covered or work paused. It has less resilience; do not promise eight slots yet. Still unresolved: who leaves, whether their hour includes setup, and which skills stay. No reply was received to the staffing question. Confirm these before finalising the advertised stations. Retain one-item screening, informed agreement, clear exits, stop-on-uncertainty and recorded handback. nodes.title: Screen twice; keep the scope narrow
nodes.detail: Intake rejects excluded items; repairers independently confirm competence, safe method and tools. Hand sewing needs an explicit needle/scissor exception. Any doubt or scope expansion means stop.
nodes.authoredText: Intake screens; repairer confirms Advertise and enforce exclusions: mains electrical items/work, battery-powered items for this pilot, damaged batteries, gas, blades/power tools, heat/solvents and safety-critical equipment (for example helmets, brakes, medical or child-restraint equipment). Exclude contaminated, unstable or unmanageably heavy items. Offer hand sewing and small non-powered fixes only. Resolve the textile tool ambiguity with the library: permit supervised needles and small sewing scissors explicitly, or offer only work possible without them. No irons, powered sewing machines or hidden glue/chemical exceptions. Ask about fault, intended use, prior repair and concealed hazards before handling. Repairer then confirms skill, tools, materials and safe checks independently. Stop: unknown hazard, out-of-scope work, missing competence/materials, unstable item, consent withdrawn or insufficient time to leave it secure. Refer or decline; consent cannot make unsafe work acceptable.

nodes.title: One item record through checkout
nodes.detail: Record consent, matching item ID and parts, proposed work, repairer checks, outcome and remaining faults. Owner stays; checkout verifies identity and explains limits, including do-not-use warnings.
nodes.authoredText: Screen → agree → repair → return Intake: one item per person initially. Assign matching numbered tags to item, owner claim and record; describe condition, fault and detachable parts. Keep loose parts in a matching container. Collect only necessary personal data and set a retention period. Consent: explain proposed work, risk of further damage, no guaranteed fix and the right to decline/stop. Owner stays; seek renewed agreement for changed work. Separate optional photo permission. Consent does not replace safeguards. Queue: match skills, avoid unattended drop-offs and pause acceptance when the remaining time cannot cover repair, checks and checkout. Checkout: repairer records work, checks, remaining faults and repaired/partial/unrepaired status. Host matches owner/item/parts and explains written restrictions or referrals. An attempted fix is not safety certification; label unsafe items “do not use” and arrange safe return, never a use demonstration.

nodes.title: Verify emergency and accessible operation
nodes.detail: Confirm venue emergency procedures, named roles, first-aid arrangements, accessible routes and seating, and controlled tools before opening. Pause the event if coverage or safe access fails.
nodes.authoredText: Brief and walk through before doors open With library staff, confirm occupancy, clear exits, alarm, assembly point, emergency number, exact address and responder access. Name who alerts staff/calls for help, guides evacuation and meets responders. Identify first-aid provision, kit and AED location; do not assume the safety lead is trained. Verify step-free entrance, usable toilets, clear mobility-aid routes, seated waiting and workable table heights. Offer spoken and written queue calls and help with forms; keep consent understandable. Agree evacuation assistance without requiring disclosure of diagnoses. Keep needles/scissors controlled and counted, tools away from children, and carers responsible for supervision. Stop all repairs during an emergency, follow venue procedures and record incidents/near misses. Smoke or a suspect battery triggers staff/emergency procedures, not volunteer handling or charging.

nodes.title: Evidence and limits
nodes.detail: Primary repair-event guidance supports refusal, one-item queues, consent, item records, venue checks and emergency planning. Specific exclusions and staffing safeguards are recommendations for this proposal; no inspection or competence verification occurred.
nodes.authoredText: What supports this review Repair Café house rules support refusing unsuitable repairs, no guaranteed outcome and one-item queues. CCF repair agreement addresses damage risk, owner presence and return. Its safety briefing uses item IDs, outcome records and emergency briefings; its venue checklist includes access, toilets and emergency facilities. HSE emergency guidance supports proportionate plans, clear roles, unobstructed exits and assisted evacuation. These are general and UK-based sources, not local legal clearance. Protected staffing, stricter exclusions and handoffs are this review’s recommendations. No venue inspection, skill assessment, local policy check or supply inventory occurred; budget remains unresolved.

nodes.title: Two stations, six volunteers
nodes.detail: Propose two hand-sewing repairers, one simple-household repairer, one intake host, one queue/checkout host and one protected safety lead. Verify skills and room permissions; reduce the offer if needed. Supply budget remains unresolved.
nodes.authoredText: A modest first event Offer hand sewing and simple non-powered fixes, conditional on volunteer competence and library approval. Role People Work Textiles 2 Buttons, seams, patches Household 1 Loose knobs and simple fasteners; no load-bearing items Intake 1 Screen, consent, item tags Queue/checkout 1 Match skills, manage waits, return items Safety lead 1 Oversee hazards and stop work; no routine repairs At most three repairs at once. Close a repair place for breaks; keep support covered. Pause new starts without safety coverage. Drop a station if skills are absent. Supply budget: unresolved.

nodes.title: Screen, agree, repair, return
nodes.detail: Use one item per person, two-stage screening, clear consent and numbered tags. Exclude powered and safety-critical repairs. Stop when hazards, skills, materials or safe completion time are uncertain; record checks and remaining faults at checkout.
nodes.authoredText: Keep the handoffs explicit Intake: one item/person; ask fault, intended use and hidden hazards. Tag item, parts and owner claim with one number. Owner stays; explain damage risk, no guaranteed fix and right to stop. Repairer independently checks scope, skill and tools. Exclude: electrical/battery items, gas, knife/power-tool repairs, heat/solvents, contaminated/heavy items and safety-critical equipment. Permit supervised needles and sewing scissors only with library approval. Repair: assess briefly; aim for a 25-minute attempt, then finish safely or refer. Anyone may stop work. Stop for unknown hazards, missing skills/materials or inadequate time. Renew consent if work changes. Checkout: record work, checks and remaining faults; match owner, item and parts. Give written restrictions/referrals; unsafe means “do not use,” not a demonstration. The focused review informed these safeguards. House rules support one-item queues and repairer refusal. Focused safety review

nodes.title: Run the afternoon; settle readiness
nodes.detail: Illustrative three-hour booking: 30 minutes setup, two hours public repair time, 30 minutes pack-down. Confirm library permission, skills, emergency/access arrangements and inventory first. Supply budget is deliberately unresolved; no purchases assumed.
nodes.authoredText: Protect setup and closing time Illustrative three-hour booking: 30 minutes setup/briefing → two hours open → 30 minutes pack-down. Adjust to the actual booking. Stop intake 30 minutes before public closing, earlier if the queue cannot clear safely. Place intake by the door, waiting seats away from tools, and checkout beside the exit without blocking it. Offer accessible routes/tables, help with forms, and spoken plus written queue calls. Before advertising: confirm skills, library activity/tool rules, insurance arrangements, occupancy, emergency roles and first-aid provision. Inventory tools, table protection, sewing supplies and tags; availability is unverified. Budget remains a later decision. No amount, purchases or funded supplies assumed. Missing essentials mean a narrower offer or postponement. This is a proposal, not venue clearance. Earlier proposal

nodes.authoredText: Make the afternoon work with five Core roles: 1 hand-sewing repairer, 1 simple-household repairer, 1 intake host, 1 queue/checkout host and 1 safety lead. Use the first-hour volunteer for setup, greeting and queue help. Avoid starting a third repair place that depends on them. Before departure, hand over tags and waiting visitors. Textiles cover buttons/seams/patches; household work covers small non-load-bearing fasteners. Both depend on skills remaining. If a specialist leaves, switch to two textile places only if two capable stitchers remain; otherwise offer one repair place. Tradeoff: two simultaneous jobs instead of three, with support protected. Close a repair place for breaks; pause repairs if safety coverage is absent. Assign names only after availability is confirmed.

nodes.title: $120 ceiling, $30 reserve
nodes.detail: Proposed inclusive caps: $40 textile consumables, $20 shared protection/consumables, $15 intake materials, $15 small-tool gaps, $30 held reserve. Total $120. These are planning allowances, not verified prices; borrow durable tools and do not spend before inventorying essentials.
nodes.authoredText: Spend to gaps, not to the ceiling Proposed allowance Cap Thread, needles, patches, buttons $40 Table protection and shared consumables $20 Tags, forms, signs, pens $15 Small hand-tool gaps $15 Hold unspent for essentials $30 Total ceiling $120 These are proposed caps, including tax/shipping, not price quotes . Borrow durable tools first; inventory before buying. If essentials exceed the allowance, reallocate the reserve or drop a station. The reserve need not be spent. Prioritize repair supplies over refreshments; promise no replacement parts. A narrower station mix should mean fewer purchases.
